description: This line plot, titled “Ablation Study on HateXplain,” illustrates the performance of different model variants on three classification metrics—Precision, Recall, and F1-score—measured as percentages. The x-axis, labeled “Model Variants,” is categorical and lists five conditions: “Model (Ours),” “w/o Prompt,” “w/o Augmentation,” “w/o Attention,” and “w/o Prompt & Augmentation.” The y-axis, labeled “Metric (%),” is linear and ranges from 58% to 66%, with major gridlines at 2% intervals. Three distinct lines represent the metrics: Precision (purple line with circular markers), Recall (blue line with circular markers), and F1-score (brown line with circular markers). For “Model (Ours),” Precision is 65.45%, Recall is 65.78%, and F1-score is 65.46%. When “Prompt” is removed, Precision drops to 61.06%, Recall to 59.64%, and F1-score to 60.16%. Removing “Augmentation” increases Precision to 63.75% and Recall to 62.63%, while F1-score rises to 62.22%. Removing “Attention” yields Precision of 64.06%, Recall of 59.17%, and F1-score of 59.67%. Finally, removing both “Prompt & Augmentation” results in Precision of 56.82%, Recall of 57.74%, and F1-score of 57.74%. The plot shows that removing Prompt or both Prompt and Augmentation generally degrades performance, while removing Augmentation alone can improve some metrics, and removing Attention has mixed effects.
